subject: Logic
title: Formal vs. Informal Fallacies
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Formal vs. Informal Fallacies.

hook.text: Some fallacies break the rules of logic itself. Others break something subtler—relevance.

buildup.text: Formal fallacies have structural errors. The argument's form is invalid regardless of content.

discovery.text: "If it rains, streets are wet. Streets are wet. So it rained." The structure itself is broken.

twist.text: Informal fallacies have correct structure but flawed content—irrelevant premises, missing evidence.

climax.text: Formal fallacies are caught by logic alone. Informal ones need critical thinking to detect.

punchline.text: Bad structure or bad content—both fail.
